rulers.name: Vasishthiputra Chamtamula (Santamula I)
rulers.note: Krishna Murthy c. 227-250; Upinder Singh 210-250. Rentala inscription in his 5th regnal year, Kesanapalli in his 13th.

rulers.name: Mathariputra Virapurushadatta
rulers.note: Krishna Murthy c. 250-274; Singh 250-275. Attested to his 24th regnal year; married a daughter of the Ujjain ruler, possibly the Western Satrap Rudrasena II.

rulers.name: Vasishthiputra Ehuvala Chamtamula
rulers.note: Krishna Murthy c. 274-297; Singh 275-297/300. Inscriptions in regnal years 2, 8, 9, 11, 13, 16 and 24; some use the Shaka title svamin for the king.

rulers.name: Vasishthiputra Rudrapurushadatta
rulers.note: Krishna Murthy c. 297-309; Singh 300-325 (the page's own list gives Singh's dates for him, its text Krishna Murthy's). 325 is the later end, used as the dynasty's end year.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Ikshvaku row. The page says only that the Ikshvakus "ruled parts of present-day Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, in the eastern Krishna River valley" and names the findspots; no area is given. In Cliopatria this land is stateless after the Satavahana row ends in 223 (7 of 141 cells before), then partly Pallava (27 cells from 306) and Gupta (87-109 cells from 347).

ledger.note: c. 325: the Pallavas conquer the Ikshvaku country. Rudrapurushadatta's reign "concluded shortly before the dynasty was conquered and eclipsed by the rising power of the Pallava dynasty"; the infobox dates "the Pallava conquest (under Simhavarman) and Abhira occupation of Vijayapuri to the early 4th century". The Pallava page has Simhavarman I (c. 275-300) already in Palnadu, in the Ikshvaku country, as a possible Ikshvaku subsidiary, and does not say how the Pallavas displaced them. 325 is the end of Rudrapurushadatta on Singh's dating.

wars.outcome: The Pallavas displace the Ikshvakus in the eastern Krishna valley; by the mid-4th century they hold the former territory.
wars.note: The page gives only "early 4th century" (infobox) and "shortly" after Rudrapurushadatta; the years 301-325 are that century-and-reign bound. The Pallava page (275-300) already has Simhavarman I in Palnadu, so the displacement may have begun earlier; no campaign is named, so no contest is drawn.

wars.name: Abhira occupation of Vijayapuri
wars.outcome: An inscription "dated to the 30th regnal year of the Abhira king" Vasusena was found at Nagarjunakonda; the page says the Abhiras may have invaded but "cannot be said with certainty".
wars.note: The infobox dates the occupation to the early 4th century; the Abhira dossier (page: Abhiras held Ashmaka, "Andhra") does not draw it. The marriage of Virapurushadatta into the Ujjain house was reportedly meant to counter the Abhira threat. No zone is drawn because the occupation is uncertain.

certainty.note: No border is given; the extent follows inscription findspots in the eastern Krishna valley.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (sa-02-b asks for it). Four pages opened (budget 2-5); "Ikshvaku dynasty" is the mythical dynasty and was no help. The page gives two chronologies (Krishna Murthy, Singh) and mixes them in its Rudrapurushadatta entry; the dynasty ends at 325 (Singh's end), which is the later bound for the Pallava conquest. The Pallava dossier (late-pallava-empire, start 275) holds the Krishna-to-Pennar coast and has no matching gain from the Ikshvakus; the Pallava page puts Simhavarman I (c. 275-300) in Palnadu, in the same country, so the Ikshvaku and Pallava shapes may overlap in 275-325. The Ikshvaku marriage alliances with the Western Satraps are reported, not drawn. The infobox lists the Abhira dynasty among the successors (occupation of Vijayapuri); the abhira-dynasty dossier does not draw it. Gazetteer names needed: Nagarjunakonda, Vijayapuri (used as a capital only); the land is Guntur 120 km + Vijayawada 100 km, the same as the Satavahana dossier's handover.
